deep.reconstruction:
This page sits in Grothendieck's preparation notes (Nov. 1966) for his IHES talk 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (notes by Coates and Jussila, published in Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas, 1968).

The first lines finish an argument from the previous page. That page looked at p-adic approaches and noted that, in dimension >= 2, Artin's observations make naive constructions hopeless. The conclusion here is a programmatic demand: one needs a definition of p-adic cohomology that is independent of the choices made (lifts, embeddings and so on). Only afterwards should one study its relations, which may be quite indirect, with the choice-dependent constructions.

Section 2), 'L'approche de Washnitzer-Monsky': Grothendieck says that in this approach de Rham cohomology 'shows the tip of its ear again'. He announces that he will explain, for the moment, how it enters, simplifying W.-M.'s construction 'to the extreme, at the risk of disfiguring it'. The simplified setting is:
- k is a perfect field of characteristic p, s = Spec k, W = W(k), S = Spec W(k).
- X_0 is smooth (and in context proper) over s.
- Assume first that X_0 lifts to a scheme X proper and smooth over S; the margin diagram shows X_0 -> X over s -> S.

One then takes the relative de Rham complex Omega^._{X/S} and the boxed definition H^i_DR(X/S) = hypercohomology H^i(X, Omega^._{X/S}). Because X is proper over the noetherian ring W and the Omega^j are coherent, this is a finitely generated W(k)-module.

The following page continues: algebraic de Rham cohomology over C, relative de Rham cohomology R f_* Omega^._{X/S}, and base change for f smooth. This leads to the crystalline idea that H_DR(X/W) should depend only on X_0, i.e. it is the crystalline cohomology of X_0/W.

In modern terms, this is the standard motivation for crystalline cohomology. The de Rham cohomology of a smooth proper lift to W(k) gives a candidate p-adic Weil cohomology, but it a priori depends on the lift, and lifts need not exist. A choice-free definition is needed: crystalline cohomology, developed by Berthelot. Monsky–Washnitzer's actual theory (affine, weakly complete/dagger algebras) is here caricatured by the proper liftable case.
errors: No mathematical error. It is a deliberate simplification, as Grothendieck himself says. Monsky–Washnitzer's actual theory concerns smooth affine varieties and weakly complete (dagger) lifts, not proper smooth lifts over W(k).
The finiteness claim (finite type over W(k)) is correct because X is proper over noetherian W.

Existence of a proper smooth lift is a strong hypothesis that fails in general (e.g. Serre's example of non-liftable varieties). Grothendieck flags it as a provisional supposition ('on suppose d'abord').

deep.surprise_reason: These are preparatory notes for the well-known 1966 IHES crystals lecture. The content (need for a choice-free p-adic cohomology, de Rham cohomology of a lift over W(k)) appears essentially verbatim in the published Coates–Jussila notes. Nothing unpublished of substance.
transcription_corrections: Line 3–4 likely reads 'quitte ensuite à étudier ses relations (assez, disons, fort indirectes) avec ces dernières' rather than 'fort indirectement) avec cette dernière'.

'On part de X_0 [-...-]' : the crossed word looks like '[-projective-]' (or similar) before 'lisse sur s'. Read 'On part de X_0 lisse sur s, on suppose d'abord qu'on puisse relever en X propre et lisse sur S = Spec W(k)'.
Crossed text after 'Spec W(k),' appears to be '[-Soit t le-]'.
Margin diagram: 's = Spec k → S = Spec W', with X_0 → X above.
The bottom-left '34' is the archive page number.
